Returns the same handle as [BackBuffer](BackBuffer). A program cannot draw to the picture that is on the screen: it draws to the back buffer and [Flip](Flip) shows it.
@returns The handle of the back buffer.
@gap The original returned a separate front buffer, so `SetBuffer FrontBuffer()` drew directly to the screen without a Flip. Here it is the back buffer, which keeps programs that select it working, but what is drawn only shows after [Flip](Flip). [SaveBuffer](SaveBuffer) of it saves what the program drew, which after a Flip is the picture that was shown.
